div.ab: [3] Kotsetlan riht. Kotesetlan riht be ðam ðe on lande stent: on sumon he sceal ælce Mondæge ofe[r] geares fyrst his laforde wyrcan oðð III dagas ælcre wucan on hærfest. [3.1] . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . [3.2] Ne ðearf he landgafol syllan. [3.3] Him gebyriað V æceres to habbanne; mare, gyf hit on lande ðea[w] sy; ⁊ to lytel hit bið, beo hit a læsse; forðan his weorc sceal beon oftræde. [3.4] Sylle his heorðpænig on halgan Ðunresdæg, ealswa ælcan frigean men gebyreð, ⁊ werige his hlafordes inland, gif him man beode, æt sæwearde ⁊ æt cyniges deorhege ⁊ æt swilcan ðingan, swilc his mæð sy, ⁊ sylle his cyricsceat to Martinus mæssan.

Cotsetle rectum est iuxta quod in terra constitutum est: apud quosdam debet omni die Lune per anni spatium operari domino suo et tribus diebus unaquaque septimana in Augusto. [3.1] Apud quosdam operatur per totum Augustum omni die et unam acram auene metit pro [3.1] diurnali opere (et de alia annona dimidiam acram); et habeat garbam suam, quam prepositus uel minister domini dabit ei. [3.2] [3.2] Non dabit landgablum. [3.3] [3.3] Debet habere quinque acras ad perhabendum; plus, si consuetudo sit ibi; et parum nimis est, si minus sit quod deseruit, quia sepius opus est operis illius. [3.4] Det su[um] heorðpenig in sancto die Iouis, sicut omnis liber facere debet, et adquietet inland domini sui, si submonitio fiat, de séþearde (id est de custodia maris) uel de regis deorhege et ceteris rebus, quę sue mensure sunt, et det suum cyricsceatum in festo sancti Martini.

KOTSETLAN RIHT . Kotesetlan riht . be ðam ðe on lan|de stent on sumon he sceal ælce mondæge ofeh geares fyrst his la|forde wyrcan. oðð .iii . dagas ælcre wucan on hærfest. [3.2] ne ðearf he land|gafol syllan . [3.3] him gebyriað . v . æce||res to habbanne . mare gyf hit on lande ðeað sy 7 to lytel hit bið beo hit a læsse for|ðan his weorc sceal beon oftræde . [3.4] sylle his heorðpænig on halgan ðunresdæg eal|swa ælcan frigean men gebyreð 7 werige his hlafordes inland gif him man beode æt sæ wearde . 7 æt cyniges deorhege 7 æt swilcan ðingan swilc his mæð sy 7 sylle his cyricsceat. to martinus mæssan.

Kotsetlan riht Kotesetlan riht be ðam ðe on lande stent. On sumon, he sceal ælce Mondæge ofer geares fyrst his laforde wyrcan, oðð III dagas ælcre wucan on hærfest. [3.1] Apud quosdam operatur per totum Augustum omni die et unam acram avene metit pro diurnali opere (et de ulla annona dimidiam acram); et habeat garbam suam, quam praepositus vel minister domini dabit ei. [3.2] Ne ðearf he landgafol syllan. [3.3] Him gebyriað V æceres to habbanne, mare gyf hit on lande ðeaw sy; and to lytel hit bið beo hit a læsse, forðan his weorc sceal beon oftræde. [3.4] Sylle his heorðpænig on Halgan Ðunresdæg, ealswa ælcan frigean men gebyreð, and werige his hlafordes inland, gif him man beode, æt sæwearde and æt cyniges deorhege and æt swilcan ðingan swilc his mæð sy, and sylle his cyricsceat to Martinus mæssan.

Rechtspflicht des Kotsassen [Kötters]. Des Kotsassen Rechtspflicht — je nachdem es auf dem Landgute [hofrechtlich] gilt: auf einigen muss er über den [ganzen] Jahreslauf hin an jedem Montag für seinen Herrn arbeiten und (oder B) 3 Tage jeder Woche in der Ernte. [3.1] Auf einigen frohnt er die ganze [Ernte] lang an jedem Tage, indem er als Tagewerk 1 Acker Hafer und von anderem Getreide ¹/₂ Acker schneidet; und er erhalte seine Garbe, die der Vogt oder herrschaftliche Beamte ihm gibt. [3.2] Grundzins braucht er nicht zu zahlen. [3.3] Ihm kommt zu 5 Äcker zu haben; mehr, wenn es auf dem Landgute Brauch ist; und es ist zu wenig, wäre es noch weniger; denn seine Arbeitsleistung muss häufig sein. [3.4] Er zahle seinen Herdpfennig am heiligen Donnerstag [Himmelfahrt], wie jedem freien Manne zukommt, und vertrete seines Herrn Domänenland, wenn ihm befohlen wird, bei See[küsten]wacht, und beim königlichen Wildgehege und bei solcherlei Dingen, wie seine Standesgebühr ist, und zahle seine Kirchensteuer zu Martinus’ Feste [11. Nov.].

3. The duty of the cottar. The cottar's duty — according to what holds on the estate [by custom]: on some he must work for his lord every Monday throughout the [whole] year, and (or, B) 3 days each week at harvest. [3.1] On some he works [for the lord] every day through the whole [harvest], reaping 1 acre of oats as a day's work, and ½ acre of other grain; and let him have his sheaf, which the reeve or the lord's officer gives him. [3.2] He need not pay land-rent. [3.3] He is entitled to have 5 acres; more if it is the custom on the estate; and it would be too little if it were even less; for his labour must be frequent. [3.4] Let him pay his hearth-penny on Holy Thursday [Ascension Day], as every free man should, and let him discharge his lord's demesne land [fulfilling its public obligations], when he is commanded, in coast-guard, and at the king's deer-fence, and in such things as befit his rank; and let him pay his church-scot at Martinmas [11 November].

The duty of the cottager The duty of the cottager is according to [the customs] that stand on the estate. In some he must labour for his lord each Monday throughout the year, or for three days each week throughout the harvest. He need not pay land-tax, but it is fitting for him to have five acres [of land], more if it is the custom on the estate, but, should it be less [land then] it is too little because he must always be available to work. He pays his hearth-penny on Holy Thursday just as befits each free man, and [he must] guard his lord’s land if one asks him [to], [and] guard the coast, and [work] at [maintaining] the king’s animal-hedge, and at such things such as should [befit] his rank, and he should pay his church tribute at Martin’s Mass.

The Duty of the Cottager The cottager’s duty follows that which is practiced on the estate. On some, he must work for his lord each Monday throughout the year, or for three days per week during the harvest. [3.1] On some, he works every day during all of August and harvests one acre of oats and a half acre of other grains as his daily labor; and he is to have his sheaf, which the reeve or servant of the lord will give to him. [3.2] He does not need to pay rent on the land. [3.3] It is appropriate for him to have five acres, more if it is the practice on the estate; yet it is too little if it be less, for his work must be frequent. [3.4] He shall give his hearth penny on Holy Thursday, just as is proper for each free man, and defend his lord’s land if commanded and keep watch over the sea, and over the king’s animal hedge, and over such things as befit his status, and he is to render his Church dues the Feast of Saint Martin.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 3–3.4. B lacks 3.1; Liebermann supplies it from the Quadripartitus (printed in bold), since the contrast with ‘sumon’ in 3 requires it. B reads ‘ofeh’; ‘oðð’ is perhaps copied from ‘l'’ (i.e. ‘uel’), misread instead of ‘⁊’ (et). B's ‘æceres’ stands so. B reads ‘ðeað’ (‘ðeaw’ misread as ‘ðeaþ’). This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4), each marked with its number.
cottager’s duty: That is, a tenant of peasant status whose rental consisted of a house but no farmland.
[3.1] This clause does not appear in the Old English. The text is supplied from the version in Quadripartitus.
[3.4] hearth penny: A tax levied according to the number of hearths per household.

the class is later called Lundinarii, their holding Lundinarium, Mondayland
Über die lundinarii Vinogradoff Villainage 153. 256; Andrews Manor 174.—Auch Leo (118 gegen 227) und Maitland Domesday 327 bevorzugen ‘und’, das namentlich aus u. 4a sich ergibt
On the lundinarii Vinogradoff Villainage 153. 256; Andrews Manor 174.—Leo (118 as against 227) and Maitland Domesday 327 also prefer ‘and’, which follows in particular from below 4a

Nicht ‘verteidige das Herrengut’ (Leo), vielmehr ‘übernehme gegenüber Staat und König die Last des Gutes statt des Herrn’ (Schmid), dessen Pflicht in 1 vorkam. Vgl. Gl Hufe 15. Auch Binnenland trug diese Last, nicht bloss die Küste

Not ‘defend the lord's estate’ (Leo), but rather ‘take on, towards the state and the king, the burden of the estate in place of the lord’ (Schmid), whose duty appeared in 1. Cf. Gl Hufe 15. Inland areas too bore this burden, not merely the coast
dessen staatliche Grundlast dem Staate erfüllend
discharging its public burden on land to the state
S. Gl Kirchenpfennig 9.—Martinus kommt oft unflektiert vor; s. Wb
See Gl Kirchenpfennig 9.—Martinus often occurs uninflected; see Wb
Das Zeitquantum wird, was weitere, genetisch spätere, Entwickelung bedeutet, ersetzt durch ein Arbeitsfixum; Vinogradoff Vill. 279
The quantity of time is replaced by a fixed amount of work, which signifies a further, genetically later development; Vinogradoff Vill. 279
Vgl. Gl Getreide 1; das dortige Zitat kommt aus Neilson Ramsey 41
Cf. Gl Getreide 1; the quotation there comes from Neilson Ramsey 41

Die fünf Äcker (s. d. Gl 3) des Kötters (s. d. Gl 5c) belegt Chron. Petroburg. (um 1126) p. 157; für Ramsey : Neilson 49; in Durham 4—7 Äcker Booth Halmota Dunelm. xxvi, bisweilen 5¹/₂ Äcker, auch ¹/₂—¹/₄ Virgate; Vinogradoff Vill. 149f. 166. 256

The five acres (see that word in Gl 3) of the cottar (see that word in Gl 5c) are attested by Chron. Petroburg. (c. 1126) p. 157; for Ramsey: Neilson 49; in Durham 4—7 acres, Booth Halmota Dunelm. xxvi, sometimes 5¹/₂ acres, also ¹/₂—¹/₄ virgate; Vinogradoff Vill. 149f. 166. 256

In der Anm. {d} bessere: 447{d}. Vgl. Gl Herdpfennig 6. 7. Dieser erscheint neben dem Pflugpfennig beim Hom. n. Wulfstan ed. Napier 170. 173. Wie Kirchenpfennig so floss ‘Herdsilber’, eine Last des geneat, bisweilen später an den Gutsherrn; Vinogradoff Villain. 144.—Laut Af 5, 5 Q erklärt Leo unrichtig ‘Gründonnerstag’, der allerdings anderswo dies Jovis sanctus, jeudi saint heisst

In note {d} correct to: 447{d}. Cf. Gl Herdpfennig 6. 7. This appears alongside plough-penny in Hom. n. Wulfstan ed. Napier 170. 173. Like church-penny, ‘hearth-silver’, a burden of the geneat, sometimes later went to the lord of the manor; Vinogradoff Villain. 144.—On the basis of Af 5, 5 Q, Leo wrongly explains it as ‘Maundy Thursday’, which, it is true, is called dies Jovis sanctus, jeudi saint elsewhere
Auch Kirchenpfennig (s. d. Gl 3, u.⁶) lastet auf freiem Herde
Church-penny too (see that word in Gl 3, below ⁶) is a charge on the free hearth
